title: Chesuncook Lake Boom House
gap: Prices, hours and eligibility are not copied here yet. We will ask when you request.
blurb: The Chesuncook Boom House sits on a high point of land at the place where Chesuncook Lake meets Ripogenus Lake. It is surrounded by water on three sides. In 1916, the house and barn were moved to this location from Ripogenous Lake, in order to avoid flooding when Ripogenous Dam became operational. At this time, the house was more than doubled in length to accommodate the sleeping and dining needs of up to 24 men.
